conviction_note: The print turns on the 2026 guide, not on Q3. The company has guided to about $100M of consolidated net income for 2026 and had $25.0M through June. Management moved all remaining land sales into Q4, after saying in April they would close in Q3 and Q4. Since the 23 July call, the 30-year mortgage rate has risen from about 6.7% to 7.40%, and Lennar and KB Home both said conditions deteriorated, so a slip into 2027 or a cut is the likelier surprise. Against that, the stock already fell about 17% from $5.16 on 24 August to near its 52-week low, the buyback is live, and Toll (a Great Park buyer) grew orders. abs_move is 7.0, above the 5.0 median because a guidance decision is due with one quarter left. p_up is 44, so the scaled number is -0.84. The findings sum to -1.9, a larger lean than the scaled number because they are proxies and the selloff partly prices them.

YTD consolidated net income is $25.0M, and remaining land sales are expected in Q4. findings.finding: The 2026 guide of about $100M consolidated net income needs about $75-80M in Q4 alone: $25.0M YTD through June, and Q3 is guided as a no-land-sale quarter. Land-sale timing has already slipped once. On 2026-04-23 management said transactions would close 'in the third and fourth quarters'. On 2026-07-23 it said 'our remaining land sales activity will occur in the fourth quarter' and declined to update the guide, citing interest rates and affordability. With one quarter left, this call must reaffirm with named contracts (five Great Park residential programs, about 28.5 acres, plus Valencia homesites 'in documentation') or move some closings into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has driven this name's largest moves. Jan 2026, when the 2026 guide of about $100M (against $176M in 2025) was set: -5.01%. Jul 2025: -14.93%. Jan 2025: +41.63%. The two reaffirmations, Apr 2026 (+0.99%) and Jul 2026 (+4.39%, with a land sale), moved little.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide was reaffirmed twice and no analyst publishes a revision. If the market fully priced a slip, consensus or a note would show a 2026 net income well under $100M, and none is visible. Pricing a full slip would also take more than the roughly 17% drop since late August, which coincides with the rate move rather than with any company news.
findings.independence: Same company, earlier document: Q1 2026 release (2026-04-23) placed closings in Q3 and Q4, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260423513937/en/Five-Point-Holdings-LLC-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results. Q2 call: closings moved to Q4 and 'market conditions could alter the timing', https://www.webull.com/news/15278768186156032.

findings.finding: Since the company last spoke on 2026-07-23, when the 30-year mortgage rate was about 6.7% (Freddie Mac, 6.69% on 2026-08-06), the rate has risen to 7.28% on 2026-10-01 (highest since Nov 2023) and 7.40% on 2026-10-15. The 10-year Treasury was reported at its highest level since 2007 in late September. Management named rates and affordability as the things that could move Q4 land-sale timing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history. The share price fell from $5.16 (2026-08-24) to about $4.28 a week before the print while rates rose, so the stock has traded this series already.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate is public and the selloff partly prices it. What is not priced is whether a specific builder has paused or retraded a Q4 Great Park or Valencia closing, which only the call reveals. A market that had priced a slip would show a lower 2026 number somewhere, and none exists.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed. The 7.40% figure on 2026-10-15 is from a secondary site (https://mortgage-info.com/blog/10-year-treasury-yield-mortgage-rates-october-2026), not a Freddie Mac primary release. This finding shares its mechanism with the builder-counterparty finding, so both are sized small.

findings.finding: Builder counterparties spoke after FPH did and both said conditions worsened. Lennar, a Great Park buyer (property records show about $121.5M of a $218M Great Park parcel), cut its 2026 delivery target to 80-81K from 82-83K on 2026-09-16, citing 'the deterioration in market conditions through the quarter', with orders down 9%. KB Home (2026-09-22) reported net orders down 12% and said conditions weakened since June. FPH's own Q2 numbers already showed builder home sales slowing: Great Park 56 against 82 in Q1, Valencia 78 against 90. The Q3 builder-sales figures will be in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Builder absorption is reported every quarter. The Q2 slowdown came alongside a +4.39% reaction, because a land sale outweighed it.
findings.why_not_priced: Homebuilder results are public, but no FPH-specific estimate was revised on them, because the only covering analyst is silent. If the market had priced the read-through, the 2026 bar would sit below the guide, and nothing shows that.
findings.independence: KB Home Q3 2026 (2026-09-22): orders -12%, conditions weakened, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000795266/000079526626000068/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm. Lennar as a Great Park buyer: https://www.ocbj.com/real-estate/218m-land-deal-irvine/ (that article is undated). Shares its mechanism with the rate finding.

findings.finding: Toll Brothers, the luxury builder that bought 82 Great Park homesites for $74.6M, reported on 2026-08-18 fiscal Q3 net signed contract value of $2.52B, up from $2.41B, and 2,508 contracted homes against 2,388, with luxury demand holding up. Great Park is a high-price Irvine community, the segment that has held best.
findings.why_not_priced: The read-through to Great Park's high-end land demand is not in any FPH estimate. The proxy offsets part of the Lennar/KB read-through rather than adding new information.
findings.independence: The Toll homesite purchase at Great Park was referenced in a search summary of FPH releases; the date of that purchase is not verified. Toll's results release is the source of the order numbers. Proxy.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-25 (8-K filed 2026-09-30), FPH renewed its Great Park Development Management Agreement, due to expire 2026-12-31, through 2028-12-31 on the same terms: $13.5M annual base fee and 9% incentive compensation on Great Park Venture distributions. After 2028, a tail of 6.75% of later distributions continues if the agreement is not extended. This removes an expiry risk on the largest fee stream; the Great Park fee was $9.1M of Q2's $14.7M management services revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The previous renewal (third amendment, Sept 2024) was disclosed between prints. No isolated reaction is measured.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public. On a one-analyst name, a renewal that extends recurring fee visibility two years may only be priced once management frames it on the call. Mostly priced, so sized small.
findings.independence: Prior terms ($13.5M base fee, 9% incentive) are confirmed in the 2024 renewal coverage: https://bulletin.webull.com/20240918/171186/bcb2bdc8f835cc79aad3afa47777531b.html

findings.finding: The board approved a $40M share repurchase authorization in April 2026. In Q2, FPH bought 623,432 Class A shares for $3.1M at about $4.96. The stock traded lower through Q3 (about $4.3-5.2) and cash was $348.4M at June 30, so Q3 likely shows larger repurchases, which management frames against the discount to book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print that announced the authorization moved +0.99%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 repurchase amount is not public until the 10-Q or release. An acceleration at sub-$5 prices would be the company acting on the discount, and no one has quantified it. The amount is inferred, not known.
findings.independence: Q2 repurchase of 623,432 shares for $3.1M is in the 10-Q filed 2026-07-24: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1574197/000157419726000027/fph-20260630.htm

findings.finding: Q3 2026 itself should report no land sales: management placed all remaining 2026 closings in Q4. Consolidated results should look like Q1 2026 (-$5.0M net loss on $13.6M revenue, essentially management fees), against Q3 2025 consolidated net income of $55.7M, when the Great Park Venture sold 326 homesites for $257.7M. The year-on-year collapse is guided and inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, a quiet quarter with a -$5.0M net loss and no land sales, moved +0.99%. Quiet quarters have not been sold on the number.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, because the company told the market. The residual is a headline year-on-year drop that an automated reader could misread.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with because the chain is unusable. The negative lean follows the 20-day -3.3% and the drop from $5.16 in late August, so part of it is already in the price. The +6.7% 5-day bounce and a low, uncrowded short (about 0.5% of float, 3.5 days to cover) cut against it, which is why p_up sits at 44 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guided range): Q3 reported-quarter finding cut from -0.3 to -0.1, because the company told the market Q3 has no land sales.

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a small proxy) plus rules 3 and 241 (one mechanism counted once): the mortgage-rate finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7 and the builder-counterparty finding from -0.8 to -0.6. Both rest on the same affordability mechanism and neither company nor counterparty has confirmed an FPH-specific retrade.
Rule 6 (unsourced quarterly bar): sizes kept capped small, with the guidance finding at -1.5 at most. The guidance bar itself is the company's own $100M, so it was not cut further.
Pessimism artefact plus rule 3 (the caveat that the selloff already priced the rate move): p_up moved from 42 to 44, giving a scaled number of -0.84 against -1.12 in the draft.
Rule 8 (thin coverage): abs_move_pct kept at 7.0, above the 5.01 median, because a guidance decision with one quarter left on a one-analyst name moves more, not less.
Rule 4 (financing) and rule 7 (crowded short) did not apply: there is no financing event, and short interest is low.
